blocks.text: A1-17 · Days, hours, routine
Lesson overview

Monday at 3.30 p.m., tomorrow morning morning, Tuesday morning: in this unit you learn the days of the week, months, ordinals and the way of saying the hour, which in Arabic uses the ordinal numbers to the female ( ⁧السَّاعَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ⁩ • the three sections, letter The third hour is the third hour. With these words you organize your week, read a schedule and make an appointment on the phone.

rows: 6–7 hours · one week (week 40 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-17), voice synthesis script, an analog clock (also designed), your calendar
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. say the days of the week and use them as a time complement ( ⁧يَوْمَ الأَحَدِ⁩ );
2. use order books from 1 a 10 male and female;
3. ask and say the hour, with quarters, half hours and minutes;
4. tell what time and from what time something happens;
5. recognize the names of months in the two systems used in the Arab world;
6. Make an appointment on the phone and describe your week.

blocks.text: ⁧يَوْمُ السَّبْتِ⁩ yawmu s-sabt Saturday Saturday Saturday Saturday (sabbat)

The week begins on Sunday, and the names from Sunday to Thursday are numbers one to five. Often it fails ⁧يَوْم⁩ : ⁧الأَحَدُ⁩ , ⁧الاِثْنَيْنُ⁩ Monday, Monday, Monday. As a complement of time the day goes to the accusative: ⁧يَوْمَ الاِثْنَيْنِ⁩ Mondays, or with ⁧فِي⁩ : ⁧فِي يَوْمِ الاِثْنَيْنِ⁩ . • Every Monday • ⁧كُلَّ يَوْمِ اثْنَيْنِ⁩ , ⁧كُلَّ اثْنَيْنِ⁩ . On the weekend ( ⁧نِهَايَةُ الأُسْبُوعِ⁩ ) changes from country to country: in many countries of the Maghreb and the Gulf (e.g. Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Jordan) it is Friday and Saturday; in the Maghreb and Lebanon it is Saturday and Sunday; the Emirates have passed to Saturday and Sunday in 2022. Before you make an appointment abroad, check the country rule. Other words of the time. ⁧أَمْسِ⁩ amsi ... ⁧اليَوْمَ⁩ Today's news · ⁧غَدًا⁩ Tomorrow ⁧بَعْدَ غَدٍ⁩ The day after tomorrow. ⁧أُسْبُوع⁩ Week ⁧الأُسْبُوعُ القَادِمُ⁩ Next week. ⁧الأُسْبُوعُ المَاضِي⁩ Last week, it was.

5. The months: two systems
In the Arab world the Gregorian calendar months have two sets of names. You need it to read the dates in the news and documents.

Recognize them enough. The first series comes from the European names; the second by ancient Syriac names. In Algeria and Tunisia variants of the French names are used (for example ⁧جَانْفِي⁩ In Morocco, a similar series to the first. Many newspapers write the two forms together: ⁧٥ أَيَّار⁩ / . ⁧مَايُو⁩ The Egira calendar (L0-10) has its own lunar months, as ⁧رَمَضَان⁩ : you will see them in A2. The dates. ⁧فِي ١٤ أُكْتُوبَر ٢٠٢٦⁩ read fī r-rābiʿa ʿašara min Uktūbar... : the ordinary is used in reading, but in daily practice many read cardinal numbers. You just need the numbers to write them.
